text:
Marcus (sales): Heads-up - Orchid Systems asking for an on‑prem private deployment (air-gapped option) with HSM/KMS integration. They asked for a pilot in ~6 weeks. Can we scope?
Elaine (product): Do we have their required QPS / models / data residency constraints? 6 weeks is tight.
Marcus (sales): Quick notes from call:
- 2x A100 equivalent nodes initially,
- Low concurrency bursty inference (avg 40 qps peak),
- Will run Llama2-70B-ish and a smaller 13B for fallbacks,
- Must use their HSM (PKCS#11) + no egress to internet,
- SOC2 + export control review flagged.
Nate (solutions): Ok. Biggest questions: network topology (airgap? VPN?), storage (shared FS vs local), and whether they'd accept a minimal MVP (no web console, CLI only) to meet pilot.
Marcus (sales): They said air-gapped for prod but pilot could be in their internal VPC with strict egress rules. Prefer pilot inside their datacenter if possible.
Amir (eng-infra): Technically doable but not in 6 weeks for a full on‑prem installer with HSM + patching docs. Fast path: deploy Redwood Private control plane as a locked-down cluster in their VPC + KMS integration => ~4–6 weeks if we re-use our existing helm charts. Full air‑gapped on‑prem + HSM cert rotation + audit checklist looks more like 10–12 weeks.
Lucy (security): We need to capture acceptance criteria up front: key rotation process, HSM proofs (PKCS#11 lib + FIPS certs), audit log retention, and network diagrams. Also review their vendor risk questionnaire. If pilot is in-VPC we can short-circuit some checks.
Jess (onboarding): I'll need an onboarding checklist for customer success: access matrix, runbook for upgrades, rollback plan, and SLA expectations for pilot. Also a list of artifacts to hand them (helm values, manifests, init scripts).
Elaine (product): Let's turn this into a scoped intake ticket. Proposal: two-path plan we can present to the customer:
1) MVP VPC pilot (fast): deploy Private control plane into customer VPC, use our KMS connectors to their managed HSM or cloud KMS, no UI changes, CLI/ops runbook. Target 4–6 weeks. Acceptance criteria: model load + inference at target QPS, KMS integration validated, no external egress.
2) Full on‑prem air‑gapped (full): installer + HSM local PKCS#11 support, automated patch tooling, audited logs, documented HSM rotation. Target 10–12 weeks.
Nate (solutions): Agree. For the MVP we need a precise hardware compatibility list and a short list of supported kernel versions + container runtimes. I'll draft that.
Amir (eng-infra): Dependencies to capture in the ticket:
- Customer provides network diagram & bastion plan,
- HSM vendor + PKCS#11 library & test credentials,
- NTP/P time sync process,
- Storage class (NFS vs local SSD for KV cache),
- Admin SSO / IdP for operator access.
Lucy (security): Also add compliance gating: vendor questionnaire + evidence for HSM FIPS/CC claims, and a signed DPA for data handling.
Marcus (sales): Customer is sensitive to timeline. If we present MVP 4–6w and full 12w they might accept staged rollout.
Elaine (product): Prioritization / backlog decision: do we greenlight this as a scoped pilot (sales‑assisted) with a dedicated small eng squad (1 infra eng, 1 runtime, 1 se) or do we schedule against queued Private work? Thoughts?
Amir (eng-infra): Allocate a small squad is doable for pilot but requires deprioritizing a planned infra refactor. If sales commits a purchase order for pilot services we can reprioritize.
Jess (onboarding): Recommend we attach a success checklist and limited support hours for pilot. That reduces scope creep.
Nate (solutions): I'll create a customer-facing runbook draft + a minimal validated config (we call it "orchid-minimal.yaml") and a short test plan.
Elaine (product): OK — action items: Marcus create intake ticket with customer PO / timeline; Nate produce hardware + config matrix; Amir list infra dependencies & estimated eng hours; Lucy attach security gating doc; Jess create onboarding checklist. I'll add a product acceptance criteria section and a go/no-go decision date (T+3 weeks).
Marcus (sales): I'll update Orchid and ask for the HSM vendor and a sample PKCS#11 lib this week.
deploy-bot: deploy pipeline check: no blocking PRs for helms/charts referenced in this thread.
Elaine (product): We'll push this into the "customer private intake" bucket and mark as high priority if PO arrives. If we need to re-negotiate timeline, propose Pilot start in 6 weeks for MVP, full in 12.
Marcus (sales): Sounds good. I'll cc legal for DPA and loop the customer on proposed two‑path plan.
Jess (onboarding): Putting a note here: for the pilot we should NOT promise automatic upgrades — manual patch windows only.
Amir (eng-infra): FYI: quick snippet of required helm override for HSM mount (to check with customer):
```yaml
hsm:
  enabled: true
  vendor: "<vendor>"
  pkcs11LibPath: "/opt/hsm/lib/libpkcs11.so"
  mountPath: "/var/lib/hsm"
```
Elaine (product): Great — Nate, Amir, Lucy, Jess: please attach your docs to the intake ticket when ready. We'll triage in the Product Triage meeting on Friday. :calendar: :rocket:
Nate (solutions): Will do.
Lucy (security): I'll start the vendor questionnaire.
Marcus (sales): Thanks team — I'll push customer expectation message today. :thumbsup:
